title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
prompt: An array of distinct integers, originally sorted in ascending order, has been rotated at some unknown pivot (e.g. `[0,1,2,4,5,6,7]` might become `[4,5,6,7,0,1,2]`). Given the rotated array `nums`, find and return the minimum element. Your algorithm must run in `O(log n)` time.

examples.explanation: The original array [1,2,3,4,5] was rotated so that it starts at index 3.
The array wasn't actually rotated (or was rotated a full cycle), so the minimum is the first element.

constraints: All the integers of nums are unique
nums is sorted and then rotated between 0 and n - 1 times
hints: A linear scan finds the minimum in O(n), but the rotated-sorted structure allows something faster.
Compare the middle element to the rightmost element: if nums[mid] > nums[right], the minimum must be somewhere to the right of mid; otherwise it's at mid or to its left.
Binary search using that comparison, narrowing the search space by half each time, until low and high converge on the minimum.

solution.approach: Use binary search based on comparing the middle element to the rightmost element of the current search window. If nums[mid] > nums[right], the rotation point (and thus the minimum) must lie to the right of mid, so move low to mid + 1. Otherwise, the minimum is at mid or somewhere to its left, so move high to mid (not mid - 1, since mid itself could be the answer). Repeat until low equals high, which converges on the minimum in O(log n) time.
